Content: Which characteristic of the passage shows that it is fiction?

Key.Rationale: There is no required length for fiction.
All genres can use descriptive language.

C.Choice: It has a conflict and a resolution.

Key.Rationale: `text(One)` characteristic of fiction is to have a conflict and for the conflict to be resolved.

D.Choice: It takes place in more than `text(one)` setting.

Key.Rationale: All genres can include more than `text(one)` setting.

Content: Paragraphs `2` and `3` are `ultext(mainly)` about

A.Choice: how Charlie and the narrator `text(first)` met in school.

Key.Rationale: Paragraph `2` mentions that Charlie and the narrator have known each other since kindergarten, but paragraph `3` mentions nothing about their history.

B.Choice: the narrator's feelings about his working relationship with Charlie.

Key.Rationale: Paragraphs `2` and `3` detail the narrator's negative past experiences working with Charlie and the narrator's relief that they would not have to work hand-in-hand on the book fair project.

C.Choice: the responsibilities that Charlie and the narrator undertake on the project.

Key.Rationale: Paragraph `3` details how the assignment is divided up between Charlie and the narrator, but paragraph `2` mentions nothing about the assignment.

D.Choice: Mr. Egan's reasons for why the narrator and Charlie are made partners on the project.

Key.Rationale: There is confusion expressed in paragraph `2` from the narrator in regards to why Mr. Egan put him and Charlie together on the project, but there is no evidence in these paragraphs about why Mr. Egan made that decision.

Content: How is Mr. Egan important to the plot?

A.Choice: He helps the narrator understand the value of cooperating with others.

Key.Rationale: At the end of the passage when the narrator questions Mr. Egan about his rationale for teaming the narrator and Charlie together, Mr. Egan replies that his intent was for the boys to see the importance of communication and working together.

B.Choice: He provides the organizational skills needed for the narrator and Charlie to be successful.

Key.Rationale: Though Mr. Egan meets with Charlie and the narrator periodically about how their preparations are going, based on the passage he did not provide any strategies for their work. He left it all up to them.

C.Choice: He serves as the adult sponsor if there are problems that the students cannot resolve themselves.

Key.Rationale: Though Mr. Egan is the school sponsor of the book fair, there is no indication in the passage that he intervened when Charlie was unable to get his part of the project completed.

D.Choice: He attempts to help the narrator and Charlie become friends by assigning them to work together.

Key.Rationale: Though Mr. Egan paired the narrator and Charlie together, there is no indication in the passage that his motivation was to strengthen a friendship.

Content: The author's use of hyperbole in paragraph `7` helps the reader understand

Key.Rationale: The reference to Charlie being surrounded by “a `text(zillion)` boxes of books” does not describe where Charlie has to go.
The reference to Charlie being surrounded by “a `text(zillion)` boxes of books” describes how overwhelmed Charlie appears in getting his part of the project finished.
The reference to Charlie being surrounded by “a `text(zillion)` boxes of books” does not describe how the narrator is feeling.
The reference to Charlie being surrounded by “a `text(zillion)` boxes of books” does not describe the satisfaction that Charlie is feeling.

Content: Using knowledge of word parts, what does `ultext(unforeseeable)` mean?

A.Choice: not able to see at all

Key.Rationale: The word “foresee” means to be able to predict or be aware of beforehand, not to be unable see at all.
The word “foresee” means to be able to predict or be aware of beforehand, not to be unable to see again.
The word “foresee” means to be able to predict or be aware of beforehand, but the prefix “un” added to the word causes it to mean not able to see the future or be aware of beforehand.
The word “foresee” means to be able to predict or be aware of beforehand, not to be unable to see correctly.

Content: :ibox:Wang Shiqiang, Wang Yani's father, gave up his career as an artist when Wang Yani was `text(eight years)` old. He did not want her to be influenced by his style of painting. He was determined for her to develop her own style. In order to broaden her experience, he took her on tours to numerous countries. He felt that this experience would give her inspiration for her paintings.
Which statement is the `bbtext(best)` summary of the information above and the information from paragraph `2` of the passage?

A.Choice: Wang Shiqiang wanted his daughter's art to be unique.

Key.Rationale: The paragraph in the stem states, “He did not want her to be influenced by his style of painting. He was determined for her to develop her own style.” The passage states, “... her father, an art teacher and painter, gave her the materials she needed.” These lines support the idea that Wang Yani's father wanted her art to be special.

B.Choice: Wang Shiqiang made sure that his daughter's art was similar to his.

Key.Rationale: The information in the texts makes it clear that Wang Shiqiang wanted his daughter's art to be unlike his own.

C.Choice: Wang Shiqiang felt that his daughter's art should reflect Chinese tradition.

Key.Rationale: The information in the passage notes that Wang Yani used traditional Chinese materials, but both texts make it clear that Wang Shiqiang wanted his daughter's art to be her own.

D.Choice: Wang Shiqiang thought his daughter's art should focus on Chinese sceneries.

Key.Rationale: The information in the passage notes that Wang Yani used traditional Chinese materials, but both texts make it clear that Wang Shiqiang wanted his daughter's art to reflect her own interests.

Content: Which characteristic of the passage `bbtext(best)` classifies it as nonfiction?

Key.Rationale: Specific vocabulary may be found in fiction and poetry.
Fiction text is also organized into paragraphs.

C.Choice: It tells about the life of a real person.

Key.Rationale: A key characteristic of nonfiction is that it is about something that exists and that has elements that can be verified.

D.Choice: It contains a conflict and a resolution.

Key.Rationale: Both fiction and nonfiction can contain a conflict and resolution.

Content: A student is creating a paraphrase of paragraph `8`. Place `bbtext(two)` sentences in the correct order to complete the paraphrase.
Which of the following is a paraphrase of paragraph `8`?

A.Choice: As a young painter, Yani enjoyed painting animals. After painting for some time, Yani expanded her subjects to include people and nature. Yani used her art to share her thoughts and feelings with others. Once, Yani painted food to tell her mom she wanted something to eat.

Key.Rationale: This choice includes the key details in the correct order.

B.Choice: As a young painter, Yani enjoyed painting animals. After painting for some time, Yani expanded her subjects to include people and nature. Cats and monkeys were Yani's favorite subjects to paint. Yani believed that monkeys were the most fun to paint.

Key.Rationale: This choice includes a couple of key details, but others are unimportant or are in the wrong order.

C.Choice: As a young painter, Yani enjoyed painting animals. After painting for some time, Yani expanded her subjects to include people and nature. Yani believed that monkeys were the most fun to paint. It was important to Yani that her paintings tell a story.

Key.Rationale: This choice includes a couple of key details, but others are unimportant or are in the wrong order.

D.Choice: As a young painter, Yani enjoyed painting animals. After painting for some time, Yani expanded her subjects to include people and nature. It was important to Yani that her paintings tell a story. Once, Yani painted food to tell her mom she wanted something to eat.

Key.Rationale: This choice includes a couple of key details, but others are unimportant or are in the wrong order.

Content: There are many steps in the writing process. `text(One)` of them is to revise a `text(first)` draft. Explain why this step is an important part of the writing process.
Which sentence from the passage contains an `bbtext(opinion)`?

A.Choice: Wang Yani was born in Gongcheng, a small town in southern China.

Key.Rationale: This sentence is a fact because it contains information that can be verified.

B.Choice: Over the next few years, Yani's work was shown throughout Asia, Europe, and North America.

Key.Rationale: This sentence is a fact because it contains information that can be verified.

C.Choice: Amazingly, Yani has never had any formal art training or painting classes.

Key.Rationale: It may not be “amazing” that Wang Yani does not have formal art training. This is a subjective claim.

D.Choice: Even when she was in school, Yani managed to paint about `text(three)` pictures a day.

Key.Rationale: This sentence is a fact because it contains information that can be verified.

Content: How does the sequential structure of paragraphs `2-4` `bbtext(best)` support the author's purpose of informing readers about how Wang Yani's talent became widely recognized?

A.Choice: by sharing the name of Wang Yani's exhibition

Key.Rationale: This information provides a single detail about Wang Yani but does not provide extended information about her early years as an artist.

B.Choice: by naming the town where Wang Yani was born

Key.Rationale: This information about Wang Yani does not tell the reader anything about her early years as an artist.

C.Choice: by revealing the places Wang Yani exhibited her art

Key.Rationale: The `text(first four)` paragraphs tell about Wang Yani's interest in painting and then name the different places she showed her art in chronological order.

D.Choice: by explaining that Wang Yani's father gave her art supplies

Key.Rationale: This information shares how Wang Yani's interest in art was supported by her father, but does not provide extended information about her early years as an artist.

Content: In paragraph `1`, what does `bbtext(culprit)` mean?

Key.Rationale: A “culprit” is a person who does something wrong rather than “genius” which means to be exceptionally talented or gifted.
A painter is a person who, in this context, uses paints to create art. It does not have the negative association the word “culprit” has.
The `text(first)` sentence of the paragraph states that a painting had been ruined. The `text(second)` sentence says that the culprit, or offender responsible for the misdeed, was his daughter.
A “youngster” is a young person or child, while a “culprit” is a person who does something wrong.

Content: Complete the analogy.
:ibox:`bbtext(Artist)` is to exhibition as `bbtext(actor)` is to ________ .

Key.Rationale: The relationship in the `text(first)` part of the analogy shows what an artist does after working on subjects. An actor performs in a play as the final step in an artistic process.

A costume can function as a tool to support an actor in their role.

Content: Where is the `bbtext(best)` place to add the prepositional phrase `bbtext(for over 5,000 years)` in lines `1` and `2`?

Key.Rationale: The prepositional phrase does modify an adverb, but not this adverb.

Content: What change, if any, should be made to `bbtext(are)` in line `3`?

Key.Rationale: This is a singular present tense verb which is incorrect for subject and verb agreement in this sentence.
This is singular past tense verb which is incorrect for subject and verb agreement in this sentence.
The report is written in the past tense, and because the subject “Egyptians” is plural then the verb must be the plural past tense form “were” in order to have correct subject and verb agreement.

Content: What change should be made to `bbtext(fat oil gel or waxy substance)` in line `7`?

A.Choice: fat: oil: gel: or waxy substance

Key.Rationale: Colons are used to give emphasis, present dialogue, introduce lists or texts, and to clarify titles. Colons are not used to separate items in a series.

B.Choice: fat; oil; gel; or waxy substance

Key.Rationale: Semicolons are not used to separate items in a series.

C.Choice: fat, oil, gel, or waxy substance

Key.Rationale: Commas are used to separate items in a series.
Hyphens are not used to separate items in a series.

Content: What change should be made to lines `14` and `15` to best combine these sentences into a compound sentence?

A.Choice: Paraffin wax is currently the most-used product in creating candles since beeswax is still used today.

Key.Rationale: This is a complex sentence with the wrong conjunction used in regards to the relationship of ideas being combined.

B.Choice: Even though paraffin wax is currently the most-used product in creating candles, beeswax is still used today.

Key.Rationale: This is a complex sentence.

C.Choice: Paraffin wax is currently the most-used product in creating candles while beeswax is still used today.

Key.Rationale: This is a complex sentence.

D.Choice: Paraffin wax is currently the most-used product in creating candles, but beeswax is still used today.

Key.Rationale: The use of the conjunction “but” preceded by a comma combines these `text(two)` sentences into a compound sentence.

Content: What change, if any, should be made to the sentence in lines `16` and `17`?

A.Choice: Although there are several ways to make candles by using molds, most traditional candles are made by `text(one)` of `text(two)` other methods.

Key.Rationale: The introductory dependent clause needs to be separated from the independent clause with a comma.

B.Choice: Although there are several ways to make candles by using molds most traditional candles are made by `text(one)` of `text(two)` other methods.

Key.Rationale: The introductory dependent clause needs to be separated from the independent clause with a comma because without the comma this is a run-on sentence.

C.Choice: Although there are several ways to make candles by using molds: most traditional candles are made by `text(one)` of `text(two)` other methods.

Key.Rationale: The introductory dependent clause needs to be separated from the independent clause with a comma, not a colon.
The introductory dependent clause needs to be separated from the independent clause with a comma, not a semicolon.
